analysis.notes: Sixteen bars, two keys. The first half is a minor i–iv–iiø–V–i in C minor; the second half jumps a half step up to a major ii–V–I in Db (Ebm7–Ab7–Dbmaj7) before returning through the minor ii–V. Because the two keys are a half step apart, the shift is heard immediately, which makes this a great tune for practising key-centre awareness. Straight eighths, bossa feel.

learning.why: A short, memorable form that contrasts a minor ii–V–i with a major ii–V–I a half step away, in a straight-eighth bossa feel. Good for getting comfortable outside swing.
concepts: Melodic minor / harmonic minor over G7
drills: Comp a bossa pattern (bass note on 1 and 3, chord on the ands) with the trio at 140 BPM.
Play C minor pentatonic for eight bars, then Db major pentatonic for four, then back.
Loop bars 9–12 and practise the Ebm7–Ab7–Dbmaj7 with guide tones.
Sing the root of each chord one bar ahead while the trio plays.
milestones: Know the form and changes from memory
Comp a bossa pattern through the form
Comp drop-2 voicings with the trio
Play a chord-tone solo over the whole form
Play the melody from memory (learn it by ear from a recording)
